subject: Post-call: Hosting qualification and audit evidence sprint backlog
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Reed <oliver.reed@everwell.health>; Procurement Team <procurement@everwell.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Sep 2025 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Hosting qualification and audit evidence sprint backlog

Hi Oliver — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed sprint backlog so we can close hosting mode and procurement questions this month.

High-level summary (from our discussion):
- Primary constraint: Everwell needs HIPAA coverage and a signed BAA.
- Security posture: SOC 2 Type II required for any hosted offering you accept; if not, dedicated VPC or on-prem is acceptable but procurement prefers hosted + BAA if evidence suffices.
- Operational asks: audit log retention window (7 years requested in call), encryption key ownership (customer-managed KMS preferred), and penetration test cadence.

Proposed sprint backlog (owner / ETA):
1) Provide SOC 2 artifacts and scope summary — Ben / 48 hours (attachment: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf)
2) Draft BAA tailored to Everwell templates — Marissa / 3 business days (attachment: baa_draft_everwell.docx)
3) Compare hosting vs. dedicated vs. private VPC tradeoffs, including expected latency and cost delta for your throughput — Sean / 5 business days (attachment: hosted_vs_vpc_matrix.xlsx)
4) Confirm controls for KV cache isolation and data-in-transit guarantees (short tech note) — Stephanie / 2 business days

Immediate ask from procurement: please confirm whether the SOC 2 summary in (1) would be sufficient to proceed with hosted + BAA, or whether Everwell requires Dedicated capacity or Private deployment as a blocker to hosted. If you can give us your procurement preference by EOD Wednesday we will prioritize the delivery order.

Next steps on our side: Ben will drop the SOC 2 summary and a redacted SOC 2 report excerpt. Marissa will start the BAA draft using Everwell template. Sean will begin the hosting vs VPC matrix and include estimated monthly unit costs and expected P50/P95 latency for your median payload.

Attachments: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (summary, scope, auditor), BAA template (placeholder), hosting_vs_vpc_matrix.xlsx (skeleton)

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0194
Redwood Inference — production-grade LLM inference
From: Oliver Reed <oliver.reed@everwell.health>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@everwell.health>
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 09:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Hosting qualification and audit evidence sprint backlog

Thanks Stephanie — appreciated the clear next steps. A few clarifications from our side:

1) SOC 2: high level summary is fine for initial approval, but procurement will need a redacted Type II report (last 12 months) and the auditor contact for a quick reference check before we sign a BAA for hosted.
2) BAA: we prefer to review Redwood's proposed BAA against our legal markups. If hosted + signed BAA looks doable within three weeks, procurement will not force dedicated capacity.
3) Encryption: Everwell requires a customer-managed KMS option for production PHI. If hosted can't support CMK, Dedicated or Private will be necessary.
4) Audit window: procurement typically requires 7 years retention for logs tied to PHI access. Please confirm retention capabilities.

We'll aim to provide our preference by Wednesday EOD. If Redwood can produce the redacted Type II report and confirm CMK support for hosted in the next 48 hours, hosted + BAA will be our preferred route.

Oliver
Chief Information Officer | Everwell Health
oliver.reed@everwell.health | +1 (212) 555-0222

Date: Tue, 16 Sep 2025 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Hosting qualification and audit evidence sprint backlog

Folks — attaching the SOC 2 summary and a redacted excerpt from our auditor (PDF excerpt attached). Key notes for procurement:
- Scope: controls for infrastructure, change management, logical access, and logging. PHI handling is in-scope under our hosted offering when a BAA is in place.
- Last Type II period: Mar 2024–Mar 2025; auditor: Rigel & Co. (contact: lisa.hart@rigel-audit.com).
- Evidence we can provide quickly: System description, control matrices, and redacted test procedures. Full report with redactions provided under NDA.

Also confirming: hosted offering supports customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS CMK) for encryption of data-at-rest and keys can be rotated under customer control; we’ll document the key rotation and access policy. For KV cache isolation, we have namespace separation and encryption at rest with per-tenant keys in Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we provide tenant separation and CMK support for storage layer.

I will upload the SOC 2 excerpt to the HubSpot attachment and drop a link to the auditor contact in the related links.

Ben
Enterprise Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (uploaded), redacted_soc2_excerpt.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Reed <oliver.reed@everwell.health>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Hosting qualification and audit evidence sprint backlog — BAA draft and next steps

Oliver — attaching our initial BAA draft (based on your template) and a short hosting vs Dedicated/VPC summary that highlights the compliance tradeoffs and operational impact. Quick points:

- If Everwell requires customer-managed KMS for every layer (including inference cache), our hosted offering will require a small integration sprint (2–3 weeks) to extend CMK to the cache layer; Dedicated and Private already support full CMK coverage out of the box.
- Retention: hosted supports audit log retention up to 10 years; we’ll provide the retention configuration walkthrough with ops.
- Timeline: hosted + BAA route — targeted legal review and signatures in ~3 weeks if we get confirmation on the SOC 2 excerpt and CMK detail; if procurement declines hosted, Dedicated provisioning lead time is 4–6 weeks for reserved capacity sizing and SLA paperwork.

Recommended immediate checkpoints:
1) Procurement confirms hosted preference by EOD Wednesday — Procurement (Everwell)
2) Redwood provides redacted SOC 2 excerpt and formal CMK tech note — Ben / Tue EOD
3) Redwood delivers BAA draft for legal redlines — Marissa / Fri EOD
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Everwell security engineers to walk CMK and KV isolation — Sean / by next Wednesday

Happy to hop on a 30-min call to run through the BAA line items and the tech note.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: baa_draft_everwell.docx, hosted_vs_vpc_matrix.xlsx
